programme_detail_official.description: The GKS Non-degree Exchange Students Programme offers financial support for selected international exchange students at affiliated universities in Korea. The grants cover accommodation, settlement, airfare and insurance fees, and the programme pays a monthly allowance of 630,000 KRW plus economy-class round-trip airfare based on the actual cost. The support period is 4 months (one semester). Eligibility covers undergraduate and graduate (Master's and Doctoral) students of foreign nationality enrolled at an overseas university that has an agreement with a Korean university affiliated with NIIED, with overall academic performance at 80% or above. Applicants must be enrolled in a degree exchange programme, so those enrolled solely in Korean language courses are excluded. NIIED first selects the universities that operate the programme and then reviews and selects the applicants recommended by those selected universities.

programme_detail_official.description: The Fulbright Foreign Student Program enables graduate students, young professionals and artists from abroad to study and conduct research in the United States, and operates in more than 160 countries, with approximately 4,000 foreign students receiving Fulbright scholarships each year. The application and selection process is administered by binational Fulbright Commissions/Foundations or U.S. Embassies, and programme eligibility and selection procedures vary widely by country. Applicants use the country dropdown on the official site to find their home-country requirements and application guidelines; countries absent from the dropdown are not eligible. There are two placement models: IIE-Placement, in which the Placement Team secures degree and non-degree opportunities and manages admission decisions and funding negotiation on the candidate's behalf, and Self-Placement, in which candidates apply directly to universities and manage their own applications, test scores, fees and deposits while IIE is not involved. The programme is described officially as 'a program of the U.S. Department of State with funding provided by the U.S. Government, administered by IIE', and candidates enter the United States on a J-1 exchange-visitor visa sponsorship under Fulbright, with the DS-2019 issued by IIE.

Assuming IIE will place you when your home country programme uses Self-Placement

alerts.message: The application and selection process is administered by binational Fulbright Commissions/Foundations or U.S. Embassies, so your deadline comes from your home country programme, not from the central site.

IIE-Placement applies to universities and manages funding on your behalf; Self-Placement leaves you responsible for applications, test scores, fees and deposits with no IIE involvement.

submission_workflow: Use the country dropdown on foreign.fulbrightonline.org to identify your home country programme
Apply to the binational Fulbright Commission/Foundation or U.S. Embassy in your home country and submit all supporting documents by their country deadline
Complete the home country selection process
If selected and IIE-Placed, submit your Fulbright application for the Placement Team to apply to institutions on your behalf
If Self-Placed, apply to universities directly and manage admissions, funding and tuition awards independently
Receive the IIE-issued DS-2019 and obtain your J-1 visa from the U.S. Embassy

new_scholarship.name: Commonwealth Master's Scholarships
new_scholarship.official_source: Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK (CSC), sponsored by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office
new_scholarship.deadline: 16:00 BST on Tuesday 20 October 2026 for the 2027/28 academic year (nominator closing dates may be earlier)
new_scholarship.application_period: Applications for the 2027/28 academic year are open as of the verification date; nominations are due to the CSC by December 2026 and outcomes are expected by July 2027
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: For candidates who are citizens of, or hold refugee status in, one of 46 eligible low and middle income Commonwealth countries and are permanently resident there, who could not otherwise afford to study in the UK.
new_scholarship.eligibility: Applicants must: be a citizen of, or have been granted refugee status by, an eligible Commonwealth country, or be a British Protected Person; be permanently resident in an eligible Commonwealth country; be available to start studies in the UK by the start of the UK academic year in September 2027; by September 2027 hold a first degree of at least upper second-class (2:1) honours standard, or a lower second-class degree and a relevant postgraduate qualification (usually a Master's); be unable to afford to study in the UK without this scholarship; and have provided all supporting documentation in the required format. There is no age limit. Eligible countries are Bangladesh, Belize, Botswana, Dominica, Eswatini, Fiji, Gabon, The Gambia, Ghana, Grenada, Guyana, India, Jamaica, Kenya, Kiribati, Lesotho, Malawi, Malaysia, Maldives, Mauritius, Montserrat, Mozambique, Namibia, Nauru, Nigeria, Pakistan, Papua New Guinea, Rwanda, Saint Helena, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and The Grenadines, Samoa, Sierra Leone, Solomon Islands, South Africa, Sri Lanka, Tanzania, Togo, Tonga, Tuvalu, Uganda, Vanuatu and Zambia. Applications from Small Island Developing States are particularly welcomed.
new_scholarship.coverage: Approved airfare from home country to the UK and return at the end of the award; approved tuition fees paid in full by agreement between the CSC and the UK university (Scholars are not liable for any part of the tuition fee); stipend at GBP 1,712 per month, or GBP 2,000 per month for those at universities in the London metropolitan area; a study travel grant towards study-related travel within the UK or overseas; and child allowances of GBP 622 per month for the first child and GBP 154 per month for the second and third child under 16 where the Scholar is widowed, divorced or a single parent with children living with them in the UK.
required_documents: Proof of citizenship or refugee status in an eligible Commonwealth country (valid passport or national ID card showing photograph, date of birth and country of citizenship)
Full transcripts detailing all higher education qualifications, including to-date transcripts for courses currently being studied, with certified English translations
References from at least two individuals, in PDF format, signed and on institutional letterhead or from an email clearly showing the sender's details, naming three referees on the form
Development Impact statement in four parts, plus award objectives, five-year and long-term career plans, a detailed plan of study and a personal statement
new_scholarship.english_requirement: No IELTS or English language test required

Applications may not be edited after submission.

The CSC does not charge to apply. Nominators put forward an agreed number of candidates and may set their own closing dates; a nomination is no guarantee of selection. Outcomes are expected by July 2027.

programme_detail_official.award_holder_conditions: Scholars commit to returning home after the scholarship to contribute to development in their home countries; switching to a graduate or other visa to remain in the UK is not permitted. Scholarship holders cannot hold another scholarship covering the same costs concurrently. An application may be withdrawn or terminated for unsatisfactory conduct, progress or attendance, or if registration is suspended.

programme_detail_official.description: The Commonwealth Scholarship Commission in the UK provides the main UK government scholarship scheme, led by international development objectives and sponsored by the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, operating within the framework of the Commonwealth Scholarship and Fellowship Plan. The agency-nominated Master's programme is one of three Master's programmes it offers, and the CSC offers around 800 awards for postgraduate study and professional development each year, with more than 34,000 people having taken up Commonwealth Scholarships since 1960. Commonwealth Master's Scholarships are aimed at talented and motivated individuals who could not otherwise afford to study in the UK, from eligible low and middle income Commonwealth countries, to undertake full-time taught Master's study at a UK university. Each scholarship covers approved airfare from home country and return, approved tuition fees in full by agreement between the CSC and the university, a stipend of GBP 1,712 per month (GBP 2,000 in the London metropolitan area), a study travel grant, and child allowances where applicable. Applications for the 2027/28 academic year are open and close at 16:00 BST on Tuesday 20 October 2026. Applications must go through CSC Central and through a nominator - a national nominating agency or a selected NGO or charitable body - because the CSC does not accept direct applications for these awards. The CSC funds one-year taught Master's programmes only, does not fund MBA degrees, and does not require an IELTS test.
programme_detail_official.coverage: Tuition, monthly stipend, airfare, study travel grant and child allowances

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm you are a citizen of, or hold refugee status in, one of the 46 eligible Commonwealth countries and are permanently resident there
Contact your national nominating agency (or eligible NGO/charitable body) FIRST and check its own closing date, which may be earlier than 20 October 2026
Confirm you will hold a 2:1 degree (or a 2:2 plus a relevant postgraduate qualification) by September 2027
Apply separately through CSC Central at portal.csccentralonline.org.uk - remember the CSC does not accept direct applications
Collect reference letters from at least two referees yourself and upload them as PDFs yourself; they cannot be sent separately after the deadline
Complete all four parts of the Development Impact statement, your award objectives, five-year and long-term career plans, plan of study and personal statement
List three universities and courses in order of preference - the CSC will not change your choice after selection unless exceptional information emerges
Apply for admission to your preferred universities in advance of your scholarship application
common_rejection_risks: Late or missing supporting documentation, which makes the application ineligible on its own
Missing the nominator's own earlier deadline instead of the CSC's 20 October date
References sent outside the online system or after the deadline, which the CSC will not accept in any other way
Applying for a second Master's degree without justification, or having already studied at Master's level in the UK
Proposing a course that is not a one-year taught Master's, or proposing an MBA, which is not funded
Choosing a university with which the CSC has no part-funding agreement, so no placement is possible
Omitting a second and third university choice, which means the scholarship cannot proceed if the first choice is impossible
Being unable to demonstrate financial need, or failing to show development impact in the home country
estimated_uncovered_costs: The gap between the GBP 1,712 per month stipend (GBP 2,000 in London) and actual London or non-London living costs
Dependant travel fares, which the CSC does not reimburse
Any journeys made before the award is confirmed
Family maintenance beyond the family allowance, which the CSC states is only a contribution and whose true costs are likely to be considerably higher
Health or disability costs beyond the assessed additional support
Course or university choices outside the CSC's part-funding agreement list
